stem: The area of a rectangle is ${=A}\ \text{cm}^{2}$. Both its length and its width are multiplied by ${=k}$. What is the area of the new rectangle, in $\text{cm}^{2}$?
solution: Both dimensions of the rectangle are multiplied by the scale factor $k = {=k}$.
When every length is multiplied by $k$, the area is multiplied by $k^{2}$. So $k^{2} = {=k}^{2} = {=k ** 2}$.
notes: Basic entry point: one rule (area scales by k squared), whole-number enlargement, original area given, new area asked. Modelled on ex13-7-16 (square, area scales by k^2) but with a concrete area so the student applies A_new = k^2 A. Both length and width are scaled, so the rectangle is similar to the original and the k^2 rule applies. Whole-number answer always (A * k^2, at most 1000). Typical wrong answers are the catalogued errors: A * k (scale factor applied once, mc:g10m13s4-1-3:scale-factor-applied-once) and A * k^3 (wrong power, mc:g10m13s4-1-3:wrong-power-for-measure). Numeric family, so no distractor options carry those ids.
